summary: XRD analysis of CsPbBr3 quantum dots (QDs) subjected to multiple purification cycles with benzenesulfonic acid (DBSA) shows that the crystal structure remains stable, as evidenced by consistent peak positions and broad peak widths across all washing conditions. No phase changes or significant structural degradation are observed, indicating robust structural integrity of the QDs during repeated purification.
experimental_variables: Number of DBSA purification/washing cycles (DBSA-1, DBSA-3, DBSA-5)

key_findings.finding: XRD peak positions (15.2, 21.6, 30.6, 34.3, 37.7, 43.6, 47.7, 51.7 degrees) remain unchanged after 1, 3, and 5 DBSA purification cycles.
XRD peaks are consistently broad for all samples, suggesting nanocrystalline domain size is maintained throughout purification.
No new phases are detected after multiple purification cycles.

scientific_interpretation.claim: The crystal structure of CsPbBr3 QDs is stable and resilient to multiple DBSA purification cycles.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: Identical XRD peak positions and broad peak widths across all washing cycles indicate that the crystal structure and nanocrystalline nature are preserved, with no evidence of phase transformation or degradation.

citations.evidence: XRD patterns remain similar after multiple washing cycles

scientific_interpretation.claim: The broad XRD peaks across all samples suggest that the QDs retain their nanocrystalline size after repeated purification.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: Broad peak widths are characteristic of nanocrystalline materials, and the lack of change in peak width with increasing purification cycles suggests particle size is not significantly affected.

scientific_interpretation.claim: There is no evidence of phase impurity or structural decomposition in CsPbBr3 QDs after up to five DBSA purification cycles.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: No new peaks or phase assignments are reported in the XRD data after multiple purification cycles.

limitations.claim: Quantitative crystallite size analysis is not possible due to missing FWHM data.
No explicit phase identification or lattice parameter refinement is provided, limiting the ability to confirm phase purity or detect subtle structural changes.
Interpretations are limited to a single figure; no cross-figure comparison is possible due to only one XRD figure being present.
